hints: Start with the normal DNA triplet ACA. Transcribe it to mRNA (remember A pairs with U, C pairs with G) and check what amino acid the 10th position normally is.
Now transcribe each mutant DNA triplet (ACC, ACG, ACT) to mRNA the same way and match them to UGU, UGC, UGG and UGA. Which ones stop being cysteine?
walkthrough:
**Find the normal mRNA codon**

Well done for spotting we must convert DNA to mRNA first. The template triplet ACA is transcribed base by base to mRNA.

$$ACA (DNA) \rightarrow UGU (mRNA)$$
That is cysteine, so normally the 10th amino acid CAN form a disulfide bond.

**Transcribe each single-base mutant**

Only the third base changes here, so this is quick. Remember in transcription, A-U, C-G, T-A:

$$ACC \rightarrow UGG$$
$$ACG \rightarrow UGC$$
$$ACT \rightarrow UGA$$

**Decide which lose the disulfide bond**

Now match to the information given. UGG is tryptophan with no sulfur, so no disulfide. UGA is stop, so no 10th amino acid at all, so no disulfide. UGC is still cysteine, so it still can form a disulfide.

Therefore ACT and ACC both prevent a disulfide bond at position 10.

options.A: ACC is correct (UGG = tryptophan, no disulfide) but ACG gives UGC which is still cysteine, so it can still form a disulfide.
options.B: ACT is correct (UGA = stop, no disulfide) but ACG gives UGC which is still cysteine, so it can still form a disulfide.
options.C: ACT gives UGA (stop) and ACC gives UGG (tryptophan). Neither is cysteine, so neither can form a disulfide bond with the 10th position.
options.D: ACT alone is incomplete because ACC also prevents a disulfide bond by changing cysteine to tryptophan.
